sources.citation: Avram, Andrei. 2020. Arabic pidgins and creoles. In Christopher Lucas & Stefano Manfredi (eds.), Arabic and contact-induced change, 321-347. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.3744529 (CC-BY).

sources.note: Nothing about stress (zero hits for stress/accent/prosody/syllable). Secondary overview: Jordanian Pidgin Arabic (Al-Salman 2013) is spoken in Irbid / Ar-Ramtha, documented only as spoken by Bengalis (p. 335); phonology paragraph pp. 337-339 covers segmental substitutions only (pharyngeals replaced/deleted, emphatics > plain, velar fricatives > velar stops, degemination sitin < sittiin, /f/ > [p] pi < fii, /sh/ > [s] su < shuu); 'vowel length is not distinctive' is stated for Gulf Pidgin Arabic only.

sources.citation: Al-Haq, Fawwaz Al-Abed & Ibrahim Al-Salman. 2014. Jordanian Bengali Pidgin Arabic. US-China Foreign Language 12(5): 331-348. DOI 10.17265/1539-8080/2014.05.001 (David Publishing).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Phonology' section (pp. 336-340) gives JA consonant and vowel tables (after Naess 2008) and then lists JBPA consonant substitutions (/k/>/g/, glottal stop lost or lengthening, emphatics de-emphaticised, /x/>/k/, /gh/>/k,g/, pharyngeal /h/ weakened, /dj/>/z/, /f/>/p/). The words stress/accent/prosody/syllable/intonation do not occur in the 18 pages except 'stressed' as a verb in the literature review.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for jord1239 (https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/jord1239) and Wikipedia article 'Jordanian Bengali Pidgin Arabic' (wikitext downloaded for reference URLs).
sources.note: Glottolog lists no references for this languoid. Wikipedia's phonology paragraph repeats the 2014 paper's consonant shifts and says nothing about stress; its references are only UNESCO WAL, Al-Haq & Al-Salman 2014 (David Publishing PDF URL) and Al-Salman 2013 (Academia.edu).
